requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
I judge the marked tests adequate for `requirements.references.outline_comments`. I did not request implementation source.

**Run formation (consecutive comments form one run)**
- `fn[comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next]` puts two consecutive `//` lines before `fn b` and asserts both belong to `fn[b]`.
- `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` has multi-line leading runs in Python. It also has a consecutive-line run in TOML and YAML.
- In `src/fenced.rs`, `fn[comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run]` and `fn[distinct_runs_with_the_same_owner_do_not_close_each_others_fences]` check where a run ends:
  - A blank line ends a run.
  - A change from `//!` to `//` ends a run.
  - A trailing opener ends a run.

**Trailing comments (a comment after other source forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing the line)**
- `fn[comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node]` covers a trailing comment after `fn a() {}` and one inside a body. It also covers `} // closing b` (owner `fn[b]`) and `} // closing m` (owner `mod[m]`).
- `fn[a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run]` covers a comment that follows another comment on its line. It asserts `first` belongs to `fn[b]` and `second` belongs to the root.
- `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` shows a trailing comment does not merge with the next line's comment: `trailing second` belongs to `fn[second]` and `before third` to `fn[third]`.
- The Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML and YAML cases in `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` each include a trailing comment.

**Other runs (next node in the smallest container, else the container, root at top level)**
- `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers a run before a node and a floating run followed by `mod m`. It also covers a run alone in a mod and a final top-level comment that belongs to the root.
- `fn[trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod]` and `fn[top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root]` cover the container and root fallbacks.
- `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` repeats these rules for Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown.
- `fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` and `fn[workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows]` cover the next-node rule in YAML.

**Markdown profile**
- `fn[markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments]` asserts exactly one comment exists, an inline HTML comment is not a comment, and the line's owner is a `paragraph` node.

**Rust inner doc binding**
- `fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level, both owned by the root.
- `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers `//! Module docs.` inside `mod m`. It binds to `mod[m]`, even though `// above inner` follows it and binds to `fn[inner]`.

**Reference counts for the run's owner under `coverage.tests` and `authoring_inputs`**
- `fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` covers a `{test}` comment above a test function and one inside the body. It also covers closed and unclosed fenced references and `{cite}`-only and `{impl}`-only comments.
- `fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` asserts a fenced `{fixme}` comment above `fn gap` is attributed to `fn[gap]`. It also asserts that an unnamed `{fixme}` is not an acknowledgment edge.
- `fn[reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node]` moves a comment between nodes and asserts the digest changes. It also asserts the digest does not change when a comment moves within the same node.
- `fn[search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners]` and `fn[search_ranges_resolve_to_comment_owners_or_the_common_enclosing_item]` check comment-match attribution through the tool and search paths.

Every named obligation has a test that exercises it and asserts the owner or outcome. I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept.

between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on

containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that

instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and

:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
